rows.description: A teenager staying up late to study or scroll finds themselves irritable, foggy and emotionally reactive. Poor sleep magnifies every problem, and it is often mistaken for a personality flaw.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A wise student in exam season keeps sleep, a walk and a meal on schedule. Steady rest often improves recall more than the extra hour of panicked study.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A young worker builds weekly rest into life: a real day off, unhurried meals, time without messages. Rest done regularly is prevention, not a reward earned after collapse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child happily reads or draws alone in a corner and feels content. Wanting solitude is not sadness, and forced socialising can feel like an intrusion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: Adults worry when a quiet child prefers being alone and push them into groups. Checking for real distress is wise, but preference for solitude is often just temperament.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager alone in their room may be recharging or may be aching for connection. The same closed door can mean either, and the person themselves is not always sure which.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who shuts the door and wants no questions is building an inner life. Respecting solitude while staying quietly available preserves trust better than surveillance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional schedules quiet time without a device, on a terrace or a morning walk. Solitude used deliberately sorts thoughts and sharpens decisions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A friend notices someone slowly declining every invitation and replying less. Gentle, low-pressure reaching out matters, since withdrawal often grows quietly when nobody checks.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child stares wide-eyed at a rainbow, an ant colony or thunder and asks endless questions. Awe at this age is simple, bodily and contagious, and adults who share the gaze deepen it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
